notes: Data came from the JSON/CSV endpoints the hub itself fetches, saved verbatim in raw.json keyed by URL: /data/benchmarks.json (benchmark metadata), /data/benchmarks.csv (run-level results for Epoch AI's own benchmarks), /data/benchmarked_models.csv (model metadata + Epoch Capabilities Index), /data/external_benchmark_paths.json and the 66 files under /data/external_benchmarks/. 70 endpoints in total, all fetched live on this run.

normalized.json holds one record per source row per headline metric. The metric field is the exact column name from the source CSV; no scores were rescaled, so percentage benchmarks are mostly 0-1 fractions while some external leaderboards publish 0-100 or unbounded values (e.g. Arena Score, METR time horizon in minutes, ECI).
Rows from /data/benchmarks.csv are individual evaluation runs, so a model can appear more than once per Epoch AI benchmark; the site aggregates these for display.
date is the model version release date as published by Epoch, not the evaluation date.

cost_usd is only set where the source leaderboard has an explicit cost column (Cost, Cost per task, Cost per run, Cost per test (USD), Total cost (USD), Average costs, Spend, Average cost (USD)); its unit basis differs between benchmarks.
rank is only set where the source provides a rank column (CursorBench, ALE-Bench, ForecastBench). No ranks were computed.
context_window is not published anywhere in this dataset, so the field is omitted from every record.
Fiction.liveBench and GeoBench publish no single overall score, so each of their sub-scores is emitted as its own record with the sub-score column as the metric.

benchmarks.csv contains Epoch task ids with no public benchmark card in benchmarks.json (OEIS Open, OEIS Open Lite, FrontierMath-2025-02-28-Public, FrontierMath-Tier-4-2025-07-01-Public); these orphan tasks are included under their raw task id and pointed at the hub URL. The pattern is that Epoch runs a task internally before, or without ever, publishing a benchmark page for it -- FrontierMath-Erdos was such an orphan on 20260904 and has a card on this run.

Model identity resolution tries columns in this order per source row: Model (joined display name), Model version (raw id_model_version, external CSVs only), Name, Agent -- some external leaderboards (e.g. GSM8K, OS World, BoolQ, MMLU, Terminal-Bench) carry the model's identity only in a 'Name' or 'Agent' column when Epoch has not joined the row to its own model registry. Without the Name/Agent fallbacks those benchmarks undercount by up to 65%.

benchmarks.csv has no 'Model version' column, so its rows that Epoch has not joined to the model registry (empty Model, raw ids only in id_model_version, e.g. glm-4.7-flash, granite-4.0-micro, seed-oss-36b-instruct) carry no resolvable display name and are skipped -- 8 such rows each on Chess Puzzles, GPQA Diamond and OTIS Mock AIME 2024-2025. This matches the 20260903 and 20260904 scrapes.

The benchmark-to-metric-column mapping is not published by Epoch. It was reverse-engineered from the 20260904 normalized.json (unique benchmark/metric pairs) and applied to freshly fetched CSVs behind a schema-drift guard that compares each CSV's header against the expected metric column and falls back to heuristic detection with a logged warning if the expected column is missing. The guard did NOT fire on this run: every one of the 85 benchmarks still exposes its expected metric column, and no new benchmark appeared without a mapping.
